rationale: elementary/calendar is a real licensed GTK/Vala desktop calendar app: COPYING holds the GNU GPL v3 text, README.md documents the build. Read as text, src/Grid/Grid.vala builds the month grid with insert_column(7) and a %7 column/row walk over a per-month DateRange, places an event into every day cell it falls on, and updates or removes it on edit - the leaf's defining core (time-anchored events on a navigable month grid). Upstream was never built or run; the target app is our own design from the pinned scenario.

scenario.name: Personal appointment calendar on a seven-column month grid
scenario.audience: A single local user on one machine, managing only their own appointments (no accounts, no sharing, no sync)
scenario.objective: Create, read, edit, reschedule and delete your own titled appointments with start/end date-time (fixed UTC+08:00) and optional location/notes on a real seven-column month grid, with the schedule persisted locally across restarts and navigable back into past months.
workflow: Open the app: a month grid renders 7 weekday columns by 4-6 week rows for the current month, with a header showing the month and previous/next controls.
Click an empty day cell (or the new-appointment action), type a title, set start and end date-time, optionally location and notes, then save.
The appointment appears as a block on the grid in every month its [start,end) span touches; overlapping appointments are all shown, never rejected.
Open the block, change title, time, location or notes, or reschedule it to another day and time; save and see the block move.
Use the header arrows to step to the next or previous month and again to return to a past month; the grid re-renders with that month's events.
Delete the appointment from the editor (probe-created records only) and confirm it disappears from the grid and the store.
Close and reopen the app: the appointments are still listed and navigating back to a past month still shows them.
acceptance: The month view shows exactly 7 weekday columns and 4-6 week rows, and the header's next/previous controls move exactly one month and re-render the grid.
An appointment 2026-10-05 10:00-11:00 (+08:00) with title, location and notes renders on the October 2026 grid and is readable in the editor.
Saving an event whose end is not strictly after its start is refused with a message and no record is written.
An appointment 2026-10-31 22:00 to 2026-11-01 02:00 is visible in both the October 2026 and November 2026 grids.
Two overlapping appointments in the same day cell are both displayed; the second save is not rejected.
After an edit or reschedule the previous slot is empty and the new slot shows the updated title and time.
After restarting the app every created appointment is still present and a past month can be re-navigated to.
Deleting a probe-created appointment removes it from the grid and from the persistent store, leaving other records untouched.
No recurrence rule, all-day mode, invitation, account, sync, notification, timezone switch, task list or resource booking exists; every appointment has a time-of-day range.
